item.research_question: Does chemical medium-range order (CMRO) exist in high-/medium-entropy alloys (H/MEAs), and is it mechanically stable during plastic deformation?
item.processing_route: Arc-melting (5 re-melts), hot-forging and hot-rolling at 1150 °C, homogenization at 1100 °C for 12 h followed by water quenching, cold-rolling (90% reduction), and recrystallization annealing at 1000 °C for 30 min
item.test_conditions: Tensile testing at room temperature with a strain rate of 5 × 10−4 s−1; microstructure characterization via HR-TEM, HAADF-STEM, and EDS mapping before and after deformation
key_findings: CMRO entities exhibit lattice periodicity with extra superlattice reflections at 1/2[3̄11] positions in [112] and [013] zone axes, distinct from the diffuse scattering of CSRO.
The average size of CMRO entities is 1.8 nm before deformation and increases to 2.0 nm after tensile deformation.
The areal fraction of CMRO entities is approximately 20% and remains almost unchanged after tensile deformation.
CMRO and CSRO share the same chemical occupation motif: alternating Cr-enriched {3̄11} planes sandwiching a Cr-depleted plane.
The inter-planar spacing of the {311} planes in CMRO (λCMRO) is twice that of the fcc lattice (λfcc).
CMRO entities are observed to be >1 nm in size, co-existing with CSRO entities which are <1 nm.
The chemical order in CMRO differs from the ordered bcc B2 intermetallic compound present in the dual-phase alloy.
item.mechanism: CMRO is interpreted as growing CSRO entities that have reached a medium range of local chemical order; the increase in size from CSRO to CMRO transforms the diffraction signature from diffuse scattering to sharp superlattice spots due to the definitive relationship between real and reciprocal space.
item.limitations: The study notes that the reason for the specific structure motif of elemental species is an open issue requiring energy computations, which is beyond the scope of this experimental study.
item.future_work: Further study is needed to reveal the growth mechanism of CMRO entities driven by mechanical deformation, and to establish the degree of CSRO/CMRO under specific processing conditions.
quotes: CMRO entities are seen directly of medium-ranged in sizes by using dark-field imaging, along with the tendency towards like-pair avoidance and unlike-pair preference based on atomic-resolution EDS mapping.
